newsitem.title: USA: Hertz IPO seen getting warm Wall St. reception.
newsitem.headline: Hertz IPO seen getting warm Wall St. reception.

text.p: Investors made jittery by Wall Street's recent gyrations are expected to give a warm reception to the initial public offering of rental car giant Hertz Corp. later this week, analysts said Wednesday.

Hertz, a unit of Ford Motor Co., is set to offer 17.4 million shares at a price of $21 to $24 each. Final pricing by lead underwriter J.P. Morgan was tentatively scheduled for later Wednesday. Trading is expected to begin later this week on the big board under the symbol "HRZ."

David Menlow, president of IPO Financial Network Corp. in Springfield, N.J., said in times of market uncertainty, such as now, investors like to see an internationally well-known company with a reputation for quality.

"Many times we have the cart before the horse with IPOs. Hertz is the horse," said Menlow. "It is the leader in its industry, the biggest player. When they make a policy change, everyone else follows it."
As a result, Menlow said Hertz shares could rise 10 percent after the initial offering.

Ford has had an investment in Hertz since 1987, when it sought a captive customer for its excess vehicles. Three years ago, Ford took over all of Hertz. But now, the U.S. No. 2 automaker is divesting up to 18.6 percent of Hertz' total common stock as part of a campaign to unlock value in Ford's non-automotive assets.
Bear Stearns analyst Nicholas Lobaccaro said the market is likely to assign a premium to Hertz because of how well the rental car company is performing as an independent entity.
"The old way rental car companies were run were inefficient inventory systems for the Big Three rather than customer senstitive business operations," he said.
"I think there's been a sea change in the way these companies are managed, and there's a lot of value in this kind of operation if it's run right," he said.
The offering price range implies a total value for Hertz of up to $2.58 billion. Hertz plans to use proceeds from the offering to finance a $460 million dividend it paid back to Ford on Feb. 27.
Of the 17.4 million shares to be offered excluding overallotments, about 90 percent will be offered in the United States and 10 percent overseas.

Ford will retain about 95.3 percent of the voting control over Hertz. Assuming the 2.6 million overallotment options are exercised, Ford will own 51.9 percent of the Hertz Class A shares and all of its Class B shares.
Hertz is ranked as the world's largest rental car company in terms of revenues and fleet size.

Earlier this month, Hertz, benefiting from higher U.S. car rental revenues, posted record first quarter earnings of $19.7 million, compared to $8.8 million a year ago. Revenues were a record $878.4 million, compared to $803.1 million.
